title: The Tally Sticks
summary: Oskar's hazel sticks keep a notch for every Hollow barge he has carried, the end of each burned with a day. The Capitol harbour-master keeps his own book of what comes in after curfew.
question: Lay the notches against the harbour-master's register, night by night. Where do the Hollow's barges come in?

clues.note: A notch for every barge taken across for the Hollow men, three years of them, each stick-end burned with a day, a cargo, a name overheard.
After curfew, a handful each month: 'Guild barge, from Ferrisford, toll paid at the crossing', and beside each the ferryman's mark, O.
Stencilled on a sprung crate on the wharf: WOOL. FERRISFORD. FOR WAREHOUSE SEVEN.
Wool and crated ironwork waiting on the Ferrisford quay with no guild seal and no tithe stamp, iron wire round every knot.

options.label: The Guild's wharf, for Warehouse Seven

wrong.cathedral_almonry: The register writes every one of those nights down as a Guild barge. Whatever reaches the Cathedral, it does not come off the deck there.
wrong.fort_ashguard: Ashguard is a march fort, not a river wharf. The register has no barge for the fort.
wrong.warrens_steps: The register books them in at the Guild's wharf. What goes on to the Warrens goes later, by another door.

hints.text: Every burned day on a stick has a night in the register, and every night carries the same small O.
The register never says what they carried. A split crate on the wharf does.

solved_summary: matched Oskar's tally notches to the Capitol register: the Hollow's barges come in as Guild barges for Warehouse Seven
